subject: Post-demo: volume buckets & context-length cost snapshot
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Grant <elliot@dataflow.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: volume buckets & context-length cost snapshot

Hi Elliot — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and a first-pass cost snapshot based on the usage profile you shared. Wanted to put numbers on the table so we have a concrete starting point for procurement.

Key inputs you mentioned on the call:
- Expected requests: ~3M inference calls / month (production), spiking to ~6M in peak months.
- Average prompt tokens: ~600 tokens (includes system + user + retrieval snippets).
- Average completion tokens: ~350 tokens (most completions are concise guidance + structured metadata).
- Context-tier needs: ~83% of calls fit comfortably in 8k context, ~15% need 32k, ~2% require 128k for long transcripts.

Rough token math (monthly, production):
- Avg tokens per call = 600 + 350 = 950 tokens
- Monthly tokens = 950 * 3,000,000 = 2,850,000,000 tokens (~2.85B)
- Distribution by context tier (tokens):
  - 8k calls (83%): 2.36B tokens
  - 32k calls (15%): 427.5M tokens
  - 128k calls (2%): 57M tokens

Pricing targets you mentioned: goal is to get to a target economics of roughly $7–9 per 1M input+output tokens (target $/1M tokens = $8) once we include batching, prefix caching, and quantized model variants. Below are first-order cost buckets for discussion (hosted pricing ballpark):
- If $8 / 1M tokens: monthly spend ~ $22.8k (2.85B / 1M * $8 = $22,800)
- If we can move 40% of workload to a quantized runtime or Dedicated capacity with ~25% lower unit cost, effective blended rate could fall to ~$6.5 / 1M -> monthly ~$18.5k

Operational notes / constraints:
- 32k context requests are throughput-sensitive; batching yields more benefit on 8k calls.
- 128k cases are rare but high-cost; recommend fallback policy (trim older transcript segments + store references) and using dedicated instances for scheduled heavy runs.
- We'll recommend a hybrid routing policy: default hosted for 8k; route 32k/128k where SLA/latency permit to Dedicated pools.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll attach a simple per-tier costing spreadsheet and a few pricing scenarios (attached). Please review and mark any inaccuracies in monthly request counts or avg tokens.
2) If the math looks reasonable, can we confirm a 6–12 month commit window expectation (you mentioned procurement prefers annual commit for discounts)?
3) Can you provide a short sample of 20 anonymized prompt+completion pairs (we use them to calculate realistic token distributions and KV cache hit rates)?

I attached a spreadsheet (DFI-usage-estimate.xlsx) and a short pricing scenarios PDF. If helpful I can have Marissa build an optimized Dedicated configuration for the 32k/128k fraction and share the delta vs hosted.

Thanks — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.com

---
Attachment: DFI-usage-estimate.xlsx (spreadsheet, 2 sheets)
Attachment: redwood-pricing-scenarios.pdf (summary, 3 pages)

From: Elliot Grant <elliot@dataflow.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2027 17:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: volume buckets & context-length cost snapshot

Thanks Vivek — that summary is very helpful and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications so you can tighten the estimate: 

1) Our 3M / month baseline is for user-facing features only (search + assistant). We have an additional ~500k background inference calls (batch enrichment) that are higher prompt-size (~900 tokens) but smaller completion (~120 tokens) — those should be counted separately if your sheet treats all calls as identical.

2) For the 32k bucket: the majority (~80%) are multi-turn support threads where we keep a 10–20 turn window in-context; those are the 32k calls and average prompt tokens there skew to ~1,800 tokens.

3) 128k usage is mostly compliance exports and run-on-demand analysis (scheduled jobs). Those are latency-tolerant and can be scheduled into Dedicated if price is materially better.

Our procurement target: we are looking for an effective $/1M tokens in the neighborhood of $5–7 for production traffic (post-batching/cache). For the scheduled analyses we are OK with $10–12 / 1M if that simplifies SLA.

I'll upload 20 anonymized prompt+completion samples to the Drive folder you linked by EOD tomorrow. Also attaching our internal traffic breakdown CSV so you can map the numbers into your sheet (attached).

—Elliot
Elliot Grant
Head of Product, DataFlow AI
elliot@dataflow.ai

---
Attachment: DFL-traffic-breakdown.csv (CSV, 1 sheet)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Grant <elliot@dataflow.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: volume buckets & context-length cost snapshot

Great — thanks for the clarifications, that helps a lot. Quick follow-up on internal next steps and what we’ll deliver: 

1) Marissa will build two scenario sheets: (A) Hosted-first blended with caching/batching optimizations, (B) Hybrid with Dedicated for 32k+ workloads and scheduled 128k runs. Each scenario will show monthly $/1M effective rate and total monthly spend.

2) Aditya will run the 20 anonymized pairs through our token profiler and send back a short report on actual token distributions (percentiles) and a KV cache hit estimate for retrieval-heavy prompts.

3) I’ll include an optional pricing ladder for a 12-month commit (we typically offer a 10–20% discount at commit scale depending on Dedicated commit and model choices).

Please confirm by reply if: a) the separate treatment of background batch calls is correct, and b) procurement is willing to evaluate a 12-month commit for the biggest discount. If yes, we’ll prioritize the hybrid scenario and quantify the price delta.

Tentative timeline: initial scenario decks back to you by Thu 11 Mar 2027.

Best — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
